newsitem.title: UK: Beckett decides not to merge UK competition units.
newsitem.headline: Beckett decides not to merge UK competition units.

text.p: Britain's new trade and industry minister Margaret Beckett said on Wednesday she intended to accept advice not to combine the Office of Fair Trading (OFT) and the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC) into a single competition watchdog.
Beckett also said in a speech to businessmen that she accepted that she should not reverse the burden of proof in deciding whether a proposed merger went against the public interest.
There had been suggestions that the new Labour government should shift the onus so that companies would have to prove that any merger was positively in the public interest.

"Some have argued too that there is a case for simply merging the OFT and MMC, and for reversing the burden of proof in merger cases. Others -- for instance the Commission on Public Policy and British Business -- had other views," she said.

"Lord Borrie -- a former Director General of Fair Trading -- was asked to examine these ideas. Today I can announce that he and his colleagues have communicated to me their view that these particular changes should not be made.
"Subject to the views of my colleagues, I intend to accept his recommendations," she said in what was described as a keynote speech to senior industrialists.
Beckett said the new Labour government would press ahead with reform of competition policy while fulfilling its campaign pledge to listen to business.
She said: "One area of common ground is the need to bring forward long overdue legislation to introduce prohibitions of anti-competitive agreements and abuse of market power."
But she said that competition grounds would be the primary consideration in merger cases under the new government. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7768
